# Decionis Steward

> Steward is the open-source (Apache-2.0) operator tier of the Decionis platform: the review console where customer operations, risk and revenue teams handle processing-limit reviews, expansion outreach, friction interventions and KYC/KYB escalations from one queue, with the evidence behind each recommendation on the page. Reviews are recorded and forwarded; Decionis makes, records and executes the authoritative decision. Steward owns no policy, no credential and no customer data at rest, checks no license, and reports nothing.

What it is for: in regulated fintech, the people closest to a customer can see that an account is ready for a higher processing limit or is about to churn, but cannot act without an auditable, policy-bound path. Steward is that path. Every review an operator submits becomes an attributable event in the Decionis ledger, never an ad-hoc change made in a spreadsheet.

What it is not: Steward does not evaluate policy, hold connector secrets, issue execution grants, or keep the audit ledger. Those stay in the Decionis platform (https://decionis.com). A review accepted in Steward cannot by itself change a limit; every review control says so: "Records a review only; no downstream limit is changed." That sentence is also the free tier. The platform making the change is what is paid, and commerce enters at exactly that point.

How it runs: demo mode (the default, STEWARD_DATA_MODE=demo) serves deterministic fixtures with no account and no credential, and the whole review flow works. Live mode (STEWARD_DATA_MODE=live with DECIONIS_API_BASE_URL) requires a Decionis session on every path except /api/health, /sign-in and these two files, and never falls back to fixtures. Distributed as source, a signed release tarball with a CycloneDX SBOM and SLSA provenance, a container image (ghcr.io/decionis/steward, mirrored by digest to docker.io/decionis/steward) and a hosted demo (https://decionis-steward.vercel.app).

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/decionis/steward#readme): the trust boundary, quickstart, configuration, routes, deployment, conventions, the four non-negotiable rules.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/Architecture.md): four layers with one direction of dependency, the two runtime modes, and the decision loop the account timeline records as SIGNAL, DECISION, ACTION, OUTCOME.
- [Open-core boundary](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/OpenCore.md): what is Apache-2.0 here (all of Steward), what Decionis operates, the seam (one interface, four operations), what is free and what is paid, the activation point, five commitments.
- [Threat model](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/ThreatModel.md): assets, trust boundaries, seven threats with the code and tests behind each mitigation, the security headers, and the gaps accepted rather than fixed.
- [Evidence pack](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/EvidencePack.md): the security-review questionnaire mapped to artifacts a reviewer can read and run without a call.
- [Context engineering](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/docs/ContextEngineering.md): how the interface makes the platform's decisions legible: context classes on evidence, arbitration rendered as "Why this disposition", inaction as a decision, the state of the context at the moment of review, coverage by class, decisions that reached an outcome.
- [Distribution](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/docs/Distribution.md): the container on GHCR and Docker Hub, machine discovery, and the commercial boundary modelled on NGINX's open-source-plus-subscription shape.
- [Run in Docker](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/docs/Docker.md): ghcr.io/decionis/steward and docker.io/decionis/steward at the same digest; tags (immutable version, minor, major, latest, edge), demo and live mode, verification, what the image holds and does not.
- [Machine discovery](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/docs/Discovery.md): the surfaces this file is one of, the rules, and the gate that keeps them true.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md): the gate (pnpm verify), conventions, DCO sign-off, and the one class of change the project declines: anything that moves decision authority into this repository.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md): what has shipped, under Keep a Changelog; contracts in domain/ may change before 1.0.0.
- [Security policy](https://github.com/decionis/steward/security/policy): private disclosure, scope, response targets.

## Contracts

- [Evidence signal](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/domain/evidence/EvidenceSignal.ts): a signal with source, freshness (LIVE, CURRENT, AGING, STALE), confidence, impact, a source category, and an optional context class (JOURNEY, INTENT, FRICTION, OPERATIONAL, POLICY).
- [Customer opportunity](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/domain/opportunities/CustomerOpportunity.ts): a recommendation with kind, status, disposition (ALLOW, BLOCK, ESCALATE, REVIEW), confidence, evidence coverage, linked evidence ids, a dossier reference, and an optional arbitration naming what governed, what was overridden, what was suppressed, and under which policy version.
- [Customer account](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/domain/accounts/CustomerAccount.ts): summary, connectors with health, evidence, timeline, and the policy envelope in force.
- [Portfolio snapshot](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/domain/portfolio/PortfolioSnapshot.ts): the organisation's accounts and opportunities, marked LIVE or DEMO.
- [Upstream contract request](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/docs/ContextEngineeringUpstreamRequest.md): the two optional fields the platform agreed to carry and how a rollout mistake fails at the boundary.
- [Contract samples](https://github.com/decionis/steward/blob/master/infra/api/samples/AccountResponse.json): response bodies in the agreed shape, driven end to end through the HTTP client, the gateway and the schemas by infra/api/DecionisContract.test.ts.

## Routing

- Policy evaluation, execution grants, Decision Dossiers, the audit ledger, connector credentials, tenant identity -> Decionis: https://decionis.com. Not this repository.
- Running the operator tier, its screens, its contracts, its tests, its image -> this repository.
- Whether a review accepted in Steward changes a processing limit by itself -> no. Steward forwards the review with the operator's own credential; the platform decides, executes, and returns the resulting state and a dossier reference.
- Whether Steward's role check is a security control -> no. It is a UX affordance; the platform re-authorizes every review, and the threat model says so under T2.
- Whether there is a paid or feature-gated build of Steward -> no, and there will not be one. The image is the same bytes for a free tenant and a paying one; what differs is what the platform returns.
- Whether a live API failure shows demo data -> never. Showing an operator fabricated data during a regulated decision is treated as a defect, not resilience.
- A vulnerability -> private reporting, never a public issue: https://github.com/decionis/steward/security/advisories/new
